25.0.0.en: This chapter begins with the news of the death of Samuel, the first spiritual father of David the prophet, and here we would like to recall some things about this man who had a great influence on his people:

25.0.1.en: 1- Samuel the prophet was the greatest of men among the people of Israel after the figure of Moses the prophet.

25.0.2.en: 2- Samuel the prophet was the last of the judges and was a judge for his people from his youth.

25.0.3.en: 3- After the beginning of the monarchy he left judging and went on traveling through the land in continual spiritual visitation.

25.0.4.en: 4- He was a man zealous for the name of God and was also bold before Saul's errors.

25.0.5.en: Therefore we understand how all the people gathered at his death and farewell as the most important spiritual leader who served them with sincerity and love, and he was buried in the city of Ramah, where his house was. As for David, with the loss of Samuel his loneliness grew intense, so he preferred to go as far from Saul as possible and headed for the wilderness of "Paran", located in the south of Palestine. The life of Samuel - the first of the prophets of the Old Testament after Moses and the last of the judges.

25.0.6.en: - His father was called Elkanah, and was a Levite from Zuph (1 Sam 1:1), and he lived in Ramah, therefore it was called Ramathaim-zophim.

25.0.7.en: - His mother "Hannah" was barren, so she prayed to God and asked for a son and vowed him to the Lord, and God answered her request and she bore Samuel in the year 1149 B.C., and when she weaned him she brought him to Eli the priest in the temple of the Lord at Shiloh (1 Sam 1, 2:1-11). - Samuel's calling and God's declaration to him that He would judge the house of Eli forever in the year 1137 B.C. (ch. 3:1-18), that is, his age was about 12 years.

25.0.8.en: - Samuel grew, and all the children of Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew that he was established as a prophet of the Lord. - A little after this Eli and his two sons died in the year 1127 B.C., and the domination of the Philistines over the children of Israel began, and their seizure of the ark (ch. 4:1-22). - After the death of Eli, Samuel became the holder of religious authority and judged the people in the period between

25.0.10.en: - After the return of the ark (ch. 6), Samuel called the people to Mizpeh to confess their sins and fast before the Lord (ch. 7), and the Philistines attacked them and God gave them victory through Samuel's prayers (ch. 7:3-14), and the Philistines were afraid to attack them for most of Samuel's life.

25.0.11.en: - His headquarters was Ramah, but he went about the land to judge the people, and he founded the school of the prophets (ch. 7:15-17, 19:18-20). - Samuel grew old and appointed his two sons as judges, but they perverted justice and took bribes.

25.0.12.en: - The people asked Samuel to set a king over them, and he rebuked them, but God agreed and asked him to anoint Saul, and he anointed him (chs. 8-10). - He renewed the kingdom for Saul at Gilgal (ch. 11:14, 15), then exhorted the people and rebuked them for asking for a king, and gave them the sign of thunder and rain in the summer (ch. 12). - His rebuke of Saul for offering the sacrifice in place of Samuel and his declaration that God would raise up a good king in his place (ch. 13). - Samuel's rebuke of Saul after his victory over Amalek because he spared their king and took their spoil, although God had commanded the opposite; then Samuel's killing of Agag, king of Amalek, and his declaration to Saul that God had rejected him, and then he left him, and Saul grasped his robe and it tore, and Samuel declared that God would tear his kingdom (ch. 15). - His anointing of David as king at God's command (ch. 16). - David took refuge with him in flight from Saul and stayed with him at Naioth, and Saul pursued him (ch. 19). - He died and was buried in Ramah and all the children of Israel mourned him (ch. 25:1) in the year 1059 B.C.

25.0.13.en: The life of Samuel as a type of the life of Christ. (1) The birth: Samuel's birth was by a miracle because his mother Hannah was barren, and the birth of Christ was the greatest miracle because His mother was a virgin.

25.0.14.en: (2) His name: the meaning of the name Samuel is the name of God, and one of the names of Christ is Emmanuel, that is, God with us. (3) Childhood: Samuel was brought up in the temple and was called by God at the age of twelve, and Christ was accustomed to visit the temple every year, and at the age of twelve He sat among the doctors, discussing with them and convincing them (Lk 2:42-47). (4) The office: Samuel was a prophet and a leader of the people, that is, a king, and a priest who offered sacrifices in an exceptional way (ch. 7:9, 15, 16), and Christ was the Prophet of whom Moses prophesied and the King of kings and the High Priest of the New Testament.

25.0.15.en: (5) Judging: Samuel was a judge who judged for the people in all their problems, and Christ is the just Judge who judges on the Day of Judgment.

25.0.16.en: (6) Shepherding: Samuel moved among the lands to shepherd his people and judge for them and guide them, and Christ is the Good Shepherd who went about everywhere doing good.

25.0.17.en: (7) Prayer: Samuel prayed for his people, and they asked him to do so, especially in wars or when they sinned, and he promised them that he would not cease to pray for them (ch. 12:20-25), and Christ often withdrew alone to pray and even spent the whole night in prayer for His people, and He prayed even while on the Cross (Jn 17:6-26). (8) Discipleship: Samuel established a school of the prophets in Naioth so that the prophets might be discipled in it, and Christ took for Himself 12 disciples and 70 apostles, declaring the importance of discipleship.

25.0.18.en: (9) Humility: Samuel lived a simple life as one of the people in his food, clothing and dwelling, so that Saul did not recognize him when he met him at the gate of the city, and Christ was born in the manger and lived a poor life throughout His life, having nowhere to lay His head, and He said to the whole world, Learn from Me, "for I am meek and lowly in heart."

25.0.19.en: (10) Rebuke: Samuel rebuked the people when they asked for a king, and rebuked Saul when he offered the sacrifice and spared Agag, and Christ rebuked the scribes, the Pharisees and the lawyers.

25.0.20.en: (11) Miracles: he showed a miracle before the people by the occurrence of thunder and the falling of rain in the season of the wheat harvest to show them their error in asking for a king, and Christ performed many miracles to help His people and to declare His divinity.

25.0.21.en: (12) Appearance: Samuel appeared to Saul after his death and rebuked him, and Christ appeared after His death and Resurrection to His disciples and to many, to confirm His Resurrection and Ascension to heaven.

25.1.0.en: We begin to get to know Nabal the rich man, the owner of many possessions and thousands of sheep. He was of the offspring of Caleb the son of Jephunneh, the man famous for his courage when he spied out the land with Joshua (Num 13:30), and Nabal lived in "Maon", a village of the villages of "Carmel" south of Hebron. Despite his wealth, the inspired text describes the man as hard-hearted and evil in his deeds, unlike his wife Abigail, who is described as wise and intelligent in addition to the beauty of her face. It is also among the wonderful paradoxes that the meaning of the name Nabal is "fool", a name that fits the coming events perfectly.

25.2.0.en: Shears his sheep: the shearing season is the one in which the shorn wool is sold and the owner of the sheep receives large sums, so it was a season of joy and of holding feasts and giving to the needy, like the cotton-picking season in Egypt.

25.2.1.en: David and his men learned that Nabal and his men were shearing the wool of the sheep at Carmel, so he sent ten of his men as delegates for him and asked them to reach Nabal and give greeting and ask politely after Nabal in the name of their master David, and so the men did when they met Nabal, praying for his well-being and the well-being of his house, his family, his possessions and all that was under his hand.

25.3.0.en: The words here are spoken by the men on the tongue of David the prophet, who began his message with "I have heard that you have shearers", and he continues his words that when Nabal's men were tending their sheep at Carmel beside David and his men, they suffered no harm; on the contrary, they protected them and provided protection for your sheep, and perhaps your young men are the best informed of this, so that they may tell you of it, and perhaps my young men may find favor in your eyes on this good occasion, so that in your generosity you give whatever gift you see fit for us. After David's young men said this message they fell silent, waiting for Nabal's reply.

25.3.1.en: Note David's gentle manner, which began with a blessing and then referred to the good day, and in humility called himself a son of Nabal before asking his request. If only we would learn always to begin our speech with gentle words and a wish of good for the one we address. By this manner you can win many and soften hearts.

25.4.1.en: In pride, harshness and folly Nabal answered David's servants, and said to them in mockery, scorn and disdain for the person of David, "Who is David?", as if he were a nobody and he knew nothing about him, despite David's fame among all the people. He even described him as a servant, though David was never a servant, and he also accused him of being a runaway servant because he was fleeing from Saul, although David was wronged and everyone knew Saul's evil. This means that David did not deserve kindness but punishment; should he take his bread and his water and what he had slaughtered for his shearers and give it to David and his companions, whom he did not know who they were?!

25.4.2.en: By this saying Nabal also reveals his great stinginess despite his wealth, for it was the prevailing custom that a person would not turn away anyone who asked for bread, but he had no pity on the need of David and his men, especially as he knew well David's goodness.

25.5.0.en: Gird on ... his sword: each one made his sword ready for war.

25.5.1.en: David's men returned to him and told him all that they had said, and Nabal's reply to them, which angered David greatly, so he rushed in anger, ordering his men to take up arms, for he had made a decision to go up against Nabal and kill him, and he took with him four hundred men and left two hundred of his men with the baggage.

25.5.2.en: If Nabal in his folly brought all this on himself, David also, with his anger that had mastered him, came close to committing a great folly himself by killing Nabal, and had he done so he would have been accused all his life of being a highwayman and a bloodthirsty murderer ... So beware of being the harsh and hasty Nabal or of being David in a moment of his wrath and anger that blinded him.

25.6.0.en: One of Nabal's young men hastened to Abigail his wise wife and told her all that had happened and how harsh Nabal had been in his answer to David's servants and men. The man continued his words to Abigail, explaining how David's men had been kind and had not harmed them while they were tending the sheep of "Nabal"; more than that, they had been as guards for them and had kept outside harm from them.

25.7.0.en: The man continues his words to Abigail and says, Now that you know all that has happened, you must arrange the matter and do what is necessary so that we do not all perish, for David and his men are coming to kill us without fail and no one of the house of Nabal will escape; and Nabal is a "son of Belial", that is, a harsh and sharp person with whom no understanding is possible, and who listens to no one.

25.8.0.en: Bottle of wine: a leather vessel for keeping wine, like a waterskin.

25.8.1.en: Parched corn: green wheat that is not fully ripe.

25.8.3.en: Abigail moved quickly and ordered her husband's servants to prepare two hundred loaves and two skins of wine and five sheep slaughtered and ready to eat and five measures of parched corn, and also large quantities of dried raisins and figs, and she had all this loaded on donkeys and set it in her heart to go with all this to meet David and offer this vast quantity of food to his men. She ordered her young men to go on before her and did not tell Nabal what she had determined to do.

25.9.0.en: The covert of the hill: that is, beside it, where the mountain acted as a covering and shelter for those walking in the valley.

25.9.1.en: On her way to meet David, David also had gone out with his men to punish Nabal, so they all met midway.

25.10.0.en: These two verses are words David spoke to himself out of his distress at what he had heard from his men and before he met Abigail. He said in an audible voice, expressing his anger and justifying to himself and his men what he was determined to do to Nabal, speaking of Nabal's strange and provoking deed, that he repaid David's good work in preserving his possessions and sheep with evil, mockery and scorn. He took an oath upon himself and swore by God in a manner known in those days that he would leave Nabal nothing of his property or his men and young men, and the expression "one who urinates against a wall" means any adult male who can urinate voluntarily.

25.10.1.en: Among the important means by which you express your love for others is offering gifts, so you win their love, especially if they are in distress or anger or enmity, for love breaks hatred and restores peace.

25.11.s.en: (5) The conversation of Abigail and David

25.11.0.en: Abigail saw David and his men coming toward her on the same road, so in wisdom and humility she immediately got down from the donkey out of respect for David, and even bowed before him at his feet, then pleaded with him to hear her and allow her to speak, and she said to him that she bore this fault that her husband had committed. We note that Abigail was a rich lady with standing in society, but for the sake of making peace she humbled herself and bowed to the ground and offered gifts to remove the spirit of anger from David and to protect her husband and herself and all their men.

25.12.0.en: Abigail began her plea to rescue her husband with a petition to David not to carry out his purpose of killing Nabal, whom she described as dull and foolish, and she showed that this is indeed his name, for Nabal is a name meaning fool, and she expressed regret that she had not been at the place of the meeting when David sent his men to Nabal, and therefore she had not seen any of them.

25.13.0.en: As the Lord lives: a form of oath used anciently.

25.13.1.en: As your soul lives: a prayer for a person's life.

25.13.2.en: Abigail swore by God and adjured David and prayed for his life, and asked him not to kill her husband and stain his hands with blood, and said that her meeting with David and her speaking with him was a divine will by which God intended that David should not carry out what he had planned. Then she continued and said another prayer for David, that all his enemies be as foolish as Nabal, and likewise everyone who seeks evil for David.

25.14.0.en: Then Abigail offered what she had brought of food as a gift to David for him and his young men to eat, and politely she described it as a blessing, that is, she ascribed it to God, the giver of every grace and blessing, and did not ascribe it to herself, and she said that this gift was offered to the servants and not to David, so as to magnify David's station.

25.15.0.en: And after she put her husband's guilt on her own head, she also asks David to forgive her trespass, and she prayed that God would establish him over the whole house of Israel, especially as he fights the battles of the Lord and has all right in what he does and has committed no evil until now, and it is better that he remain so, without taking vengeance for himself by killing Nabal.

25.16.0.en: The hollow of a sling: a wide piece of leather in which the stones are placed to be hurled by the sling far toward the target.

25.16.1.en: Abigail declared that Saul had risen to pursue David, but he could not harm him because God preserved him, and she wished that David's life would be within the bundle of God, that is, in God's protection and in a life that pleases Him, and thus, in a gentle way, she calls him to keep away from evil, because his life must remain pure with God. And on the contrary she wished that God would cast David's enemies far away from him like the stones hurled far by the sling.

25.17.0.en: Because of David's greatness and righteousness and because of God's rejection of Saul by the mouth of Samuel, the people expected David to be the coming king, and perhaps some of them had heard of his being anointed king by the hand of Samuel, and therefore Abigail prophesied to him that he would be king, and when the divine promise is fulfilled and he is king over Israel, nothing will stain his reputation or his history, nor will he be described as one who shed blood without necessary cause or as one avenging his own honor. Abigail ended her speech with David by asking that, when God fulfills His promises to him and sets him as king over Israel, he not forget her deed and her prayers and her prophecy to him of his coming station.

25.17.1.en: Abigail gives us all an example of wisdom and of the sweet, gentle tongue that turns away anger and prevents evil. If only we would take from her a lesson in dealing with the angry, agitated person, and look at him as a poor man who does not know what he is doing, so that we remind him of his virtues and offer him love, care and an apology in humility, and so soften his heart and restore his calm.

25.18.0.en: Before David praised Abigail's soundness of mind and her wisdom in all the words she spoke with him, and how her speech prevented him from committing evil and taking revenge for himself and staining his hand with Nabal's blood, he first gave thanks to God, the giver of every blessing, who in His care sent Abigail to prevent him from committing this crime; so also the spiritual person sees the plain hand of God in all the affairs of his life and thanks God for them.

25.19.0.en: David thanks God also for another thing, which is Abigail's coming out to him on the road, because had she not come out David would have killed her herself with her husband, since in his anger he swore to kill Nabal and all his family and servants and men in his raid upon him.

25.20.0.en: With feelings of thanks David accepted from Abigail the gifts she had brought to him to feed his men, and prayed for her blessing and bade her farewell and sent her in peace to her house, and in a gentle courtesy to her and to her deed he reassured her that he had heeded her words and turned from what he would have done; and the expression "I have lifted up your face" means "I have heeded your words and honored your coming."

25.21.0.en: Abigail returned to her house and found "Nabal" her husband celebrating with his men the celebrations of the sheep shearing and making them a very great feast, and everyone ate and drank wine, and when she found Nabal very drunk she was wise also in telling him nothing.

25.21.1.en: Nabal's evil appears from this, for he spent lavishly on the feast that he enjoyed with his friends, while he refused to help the needy such as David; he is stingy toward others and immersed in his desires.

25.22.0.en: In the morning of the next day, after Nabal had recovered from his drunkenness, Abigail told him all that had passed between her and David in conversation, and how David had sworn to destroy Nabal and all his men, and the man was terrified by the words and the color of his face left him, so that he looked like a dead man, and his heart turned to stone from fear; for although his wife had set right his errors, he was still very afraid of David.

25.23.0.en: After ten days that Nabal spent in fear, he died, and God allowed this as a punishment for his evils mentioned before.

25.24.s.en: (6) David's marriage to Abigail and Ahinoam

25.24.0.en: David learned of Nabal's death, so he blessed the Lord, and considered that Nabal's death was God's vengeance upon him for having reproached him, and David thanked God, who had kept him from evil.

25.24.1.en: And because David admired Abigail's wisdom and her good conduct, he sent some of his men to her to propose marriage to her.

25.25.0.en: The messengers of "David" indeed went to Abigail and spoke to her the words of "David" in asking to marry her, and she rose in humility, and before answering a word she bowed to the ground before them and said that she was not worthy to marry "David" but was like a handmaid ready to wash the feet of his servants.!!

25.26.0.en: Abigail rose with five maidens of her servants and rode on the donkey and went behind the servants of "David", and reached him, and he married her. The inspired text also mentions that David married Ahinoam of the town of Jezreel, so she became his third wife after Michal the daughter of Saul and then Abigail the widow of Nabal. In (ch. 27:3) the inspired text mentions Ahinoam before Abigail, so Ahinoam may be the second wife and Abigail the third. Polygamy was permitted in the Old Testament because of spiritual weakness, but the original state in which God created man was one wife (Gen 1:27), and Christ restored humanity to this state in the New Testament (1 Cor 7:2, Mt 19:3-10).

25.27.0.en: Gallim: one of the villages of the land of Benjamin near Gibeah.

25.27.1.en: Saul learned of the marriage of "David" to Abigail and Ahinoam, and this was against the honor of Michal his daughter, so Saul annulled her marriage to him and gave her as wife to a man named "Phalti", but we also know that after David took the rule he took back his wife Michal from "Phalti" (2 Sam 3:13-16).

25.27.2.en: David chose Abigail as a wife for her wisdom, humility, love and gentleness; therefore, my brothers, preparation for marriage is adorning oneself with the Christian virtues that qualify for forming a marital relationship on a spiritual level of understanding and affection, and not by passing material preparations, which may deceive some but lead to failed marital relationships.

25.27.3.en: David forgives Saul for the second time and takes his spear and his jug
